      How plans are costed

      Each lever has an indicative capital cost, a yearly running cost and a lead time before it is in service. Plans are compared on capital plus five years of running cost, in QAR millions. Figures are placeholders until GAC programme costs are connected.

        Three ways to reach the goal

        Average time in porttodaygoal

        WASL, the Abu Samra twin

        A live simulation of every truck through Abu Samra on a true-scale 3D model of the port. Watch today, test tomorrow, and pick the plan that gets you there.

        1. Watch it live. The live panel ] shows occupancy, plate reads and any truck's journey. Filters focus the map on a country, lane, cargo or AEO status, and show what the trucks held at the bottleneck have in common.
        2. Ask what-if. In the planner [ move a slider, or type the change in Text to map. New lanes, bays and ramps appear gold on the map; removed ones turn red. Run the forecast to compare a full day with the baseline.
        3. Seek a goal. Set the average time in port you want. Goal seek returns three costed plans (fast, balanced, cost-smart) with their effect over the next three years.
        4. See the plan. Press Visualize in the twin and the port rebuilds itself with that plan's changes.
        5. Look around. Left-drag orbits, right-drag pans, the wheel zooms, space pauses. Click any truck to follow it.
